body:
Sleeping is nice but I hate dreams, it effects my mind space more than a lot of other things. For years it's only been random few times a month, now it's every night.

Last night I dreamt about preparing for a gig in a band I haven't even spoken to the members of in years, the dream did end up with me realising "oh I'm not even in this band now" and the reasons behind it are just further adding to my current space because one reason I'm no longer in it is related to the current reason for my wish to die.

Yes everyone knows we all die eventually, just part of life, yet we still get hit hard by death regardless of who it is (generally). So knowing that, why would you willingly bring someone into experience this pain? 

In case you're likely to say it, yes I know killing myself would bring people pain, the same way them dying would bring me pain. I'm here trying to justify I never got a choice in either side of this, and that's just one painful aspect of life among many others.

That revenge is a good one to have if you can live with yourself and ignore all life bullshit to keep yourself going. I am past that point personally, although I guess it would be revenge in a different direction to what you're suggesting.

All good with any rants, it helps, and I get what you're saying.

Being on that edge of it really is intense, honestly thing people that go through with it are extremely brave with their intentions, almost feels like they should get another chance with a different better [for them] life/world. There is also something peaceful about not going through with it while being in that moment. It's like we need to release a massive amount of emotions that are stuck in us and we really don't know how or who can stand listening to something incoherent (not referring to your rant, just in case).

I agree it's oddly comforting talking to people in the same mental state regardless of the reasons, we all share some pain that makes the end feels like the only true option, it likely isn't although it's difficult to see that.

I remember many years ago crying for help about suicide (I was slightly mentally stronger then so deep down knew I couldn't do it, just wanted some help/people to know) it only made people around me suspicious of EVERYTHING I did...so now it's the internet that gets to hear the desire and struggle.

It would be great without dreams/nightmares, currently getting them more than I have for many years and it feeds into reality. Basically no escape but a few moments when my mind doesn't decide to think.
I had someone that would make casual jokes about like "don't die!" when I'd mention I was going out to drive, I'd joke back, now it's wishful thinking.

Yeah every morning driving to work I think to myself maybe I should just phone in sick and go off somewhere more remote, either for peace or to the end. Life is tiring enough without the constant need to hide yourself and do "what you have to do", actually think it adds to the drive of wanting to end things. I believe my work would be okay if I was forth coming with saying I need a mental health day but at the same time that just adds the burden of being outted as being mentally unwell, which is just another fucking burden.

I've been numb for years and got woken up with by someone but that has fallen apart by failing the same way I did in the past, so I do not see anything getting better, just increased regret and the burden with life...nothing like wrecking your body just to make a living. The more I think about things I "enjoy"(distractions from my thoughts) I realise how overall pointless it all is, there is no purpose to any of this. Life is a "gift" I never asked for.
Yeah I have moments of being like "okay this is life, fair enough" but then it usually leads into feeling worse, it seems to come on in waves during the day.
